about: I got into computers because I wanted to understand how things actually work — not just how to use them. That curiosity led me to build things end to end: from the database schema to the API contract to the UI that talks to both.

Lately, that curiosity has pulled me toward agentic AI. The question that keeps me up: how do you give an LLM real power without letting it make irreversible mistakes? My project Gatekeeper is my answer so far — the model proposes, a rules engine decides. Zero hallucinated executions on critical actions.
I learn project-first. Every meaningful insight I have came from shipping something and hitting a wall I had to actually climb.

projects.title: Gatekeeper
projects.short_description: A secure AI agent workflow — the LLM proposes, a rules engine decides. 0% hallucinated executions.
projects.outcome: 0% hallucinated execution rate on critical actions. 99% structured-output parse success.
projects.problem: Fully autonomous LLM agents hallucinate. Giving them direct access to execute critical actions (payments, DB deletes) is a security risk.
projects.architecture: Multi-layered agent system: LLM proposes actions via Tool Use, a deterministic rules-engine validates all parameters before execution.
projects.key_challenge: Ensuring the LLM outputs structured, perfectly formatted data that the rule engine could parse without crashing.
projects.solution: Anthropic's Claude API with strict Pydantic schemas to force structured JSON outputs, combined with a retry-loop for self-correction.
projects.reflection: Combining deterministic code with probabilistic AI yields the safest production systems.

projects.title: TaskFlow
projects.short_description: Full-stack task manager with Kanban boards, real-time analytics, and user auth.
projects.outcome: Sub-100ms UI response with zero-latency feel and robust data persistence.
projects.problem: Teams struggle to track project progress without complex enterprise tools.
projects.architecture: React state synchronized with Express/MongoDB backend. JWT session management.
projects.key_challenge: Smooth drag-and-drop Kanban with optimistic UI updates synced flawlessly to backend.
projects.solution: State synchronization layer that locally updates the board instantly, falling back gracefully if the API request fails.
projects.reflection: I'd implement WebSockets for true multi-player collaboration if I rebuilt this today.

projects.title: Socially
projects.short_description: Private organizational social network with department-level restricted channels.
projects.outcome: Highly secure, performant feed. Security enforced at the database layer via RLS.
projects.problem: Organizations need a secure internal way to share updates without public social media.
projects.architecture: React frontend integrated with Supabase BaaS, utilizing Row Level Security (RLS) policies.
projects.key_challenge: Database schema that strictly enforced viewing permissions based on department and role.
projects.solution: Supabase PostgreSQL RLS policies — users can only query posts belonging to their authorized channels.
projects.reflection: Pushing security down to the database layer is more robust than handling it all in application logic.
